newsitem.title: CHINA: China slams Hong Kong's Lee for Clinton meeting.
newsitem.headline: China slams Hong Kong's Lee for Clinton meeting.

text.p: China on Tuesday accused Martin Lee, a leader of Hong Kong's democracy movement, of trying to incite international forces to meddle in Hong Kong affairs.

The Hong Kong legislator's recent visit to the United States and a planned meeting with U.S. President Bill Clinton was part of an attempt to win political capital, Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told a news briefing.
"Li Zongming (Martin Lee) incites international forces everywhere to meddle in Hong Kong affairs," Shen said when asked about Lee's planned meeting with Clinton in Washington this week.
"He depends on foreigners to interfere in Hong Kong issues and indulges in spreading rumours and lies to try to blacken Hong Kong," Shen said.
President Bill Clinton is to meet later this week with Lee, who held talks with U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright on Monday.
"I think he mainly wants to fish for capital for himself," Shen said of the Hong Kong legislator and a leading pro-democracy campaigner who heads the colony's Democratic Party.
After meeting Albright on Monday, Lee reaffirmed support for continued Most Favoured Nation trade status for China. Washington reviews that trading status each year.

Albright had assured Lee of "strong U.S. support for continued full political and civil rights and the way of life of the people of Hong Kong", State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said after the 40-minute meeting.
Lee is on a lobbying trip to Washington ahead of July 1, when Hong Kong reverts to China's control under a 1984 Sino-British agreement.

As the transition nears, there is rising concern in the United States as well as in Hong Kong that China is not living up to its promises to permit the territory to function as it has, with considerable civil and political freedoms.
Increasing numbers of U.S. lawmakers have questioned whether MFN, which grants favourable U.S. trade benefits to countries, should be renewed.
